notes:
I couldn't write the Hosea 13 notes this time, because the research tools stopped working before I read any sources.

My first attempt to fetch pages failed on a bug in my own code, and the system then ended my access to the research tool for this turn. I tried to fetch these pages but never got their content:

- https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-13/
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/hosea/13.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/hosea/13.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/hosea/13.htm
- https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-13-commentary
- https://netbible.org/bible/Hosea+13

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Since I read nothing, any notes I wrote now would come from memory rather than these sources, so I've left them out.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start over. I'll read the pages above first, then look for where the traditions differ. The likely places are:
- **v. 14:** whether it's a promise of rescue or a threat, how Paul uses it in 1 Corinthians 15, and what "compassion is hidden" means.
- **v. 2:** whether the Hebrew means people sacrificing humans or people (men) kissing the calves.
- **v. 11:** whether the king is Saul or Israel's last kings.

I'd also check the Lutheran, Wesleyan, Catholic and Orthodox sites for comments on v. 14.
